case_anchor: The original answer looked coherent enough to accept. It stopped one big recommendation from flattening different decision types into the same treatment. Separate the reversible experiment from the irreversible commitment. Sort the situation into buckets before deciding what each bucket needs.
do_not_overlearn: This lesson does not prove the original answer was wrong or the revised answer was right.
It teaches a reasoning move and a model relationship; it does not authorize a decision.
This product page is not a Decision Work brief and does not authorize action.

model_stack.teaching_name: Sort The Case Before Judging It
model_stack.teaching_note: When repeated decisions are vulnerable to inconsistent in-the-moment exceptions, use category decisions to define stable buckets and boundaries before evaluating individual cases, while checking that the category still matches the underlying situation.

model_stack.boundary: Simplification would remove the causal structure, nuance, or thresholds needed to make a real decision rather than merely creating a feeling of clarity.
model_stack.teaching_note: When complexity, stress, or presentation design is overloading working memory, simplify sequence and format so attention goes to the next useful distinction while preserving the causal cues needed for correct action.

model_stack.boundary: Optionality has become a permanent excuse not to commit even after evidence has clarified which path has the best economics or strategic fit.
model_stack.teaching_note: When an important decision has collapsed into a do-or-do-not frame, separate invention from evaluation: generate at least three viable options, then compare benefits, costs, payoffs, and probabilities before choosing.

practice_rep.prompt: Sort The Case Before Judging It
practice_rep.user_action: Name the tempting first read. Which category does this part belong to, and does that category need a different rule? Name the boundary that would change confidence.

relation_story: Cognitive Load Theory and Optionality form a structured tension pair. Cognitive Load Theory conflicts with Optionality when too many parallel branches exceed practical decision bandwidth. Use the pair as a calibration exercise: do not maximize either lens. Cognitive Load Theory protects against overload, while Optionality protects against premature closure. The lesson is to choose the smallest set of options that still preserves learning.
thinking_move: Sort the situation into buckets before deciding what each bucket needs.
